title: Chart spec
description: A declarative description of one chart card: a title, an optional headline KPI, and a line or bar chart of up to 12 series over time. Pass it as the second argument to StripeCharts.render(element, spec). Unknown fields are rejected. A comparison series (for example last year) lines up with the primary series by position, not by calendar date: the i-th point of every series is drawn in the same x slot, so put the days you want compared at the same index.

title.description: Card title shown at the top, for example "Gross volume". Plain text; markup is shown literally.

description.description: Optional one-line subtitle under the title, for example "the reporting period". Plain text.

format.description: How values (KPI, axis ticks, tooltip) are formatted. Defaults to {"style": "number"}. Choose by the "style" field.

maximumFractionDigits.description: Optional maximum number of decimals to show, 0 to 20. Defaults to 2.

oneOf.description: Money. The currency decides the decimals shown, so JPY shows none; amounts of 1,000 or more are shown in whole units.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, any case, for example "usd" or "JPY".

unit.description: Required. "minor" if values are in the currency's smallest unit, as Stripe API amounts are (1999 means $19.99, ¥1,999, or 1.999 KWD); "major" if they are already in major units (19.99 means $19.99).

oneOf.description: Percentages. A KPI change is always relative: 2.07% against 2.01% shows as +3.0%, not +0.06 points.

maximumFractionDigits.description: Optional maximum number of decimals in the percentage, 0 to 20. Defaults to 1.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag used for number and date formatting, for example "en-US" or "ja-JP". Defaults to "en-US".

timeZone.description: IANA time zone, for example "America/New_York", used to display date-time x values. Required when any x is a date-time: use the zone the data was reported in, or "UTC". Date-only values like "2026-11-27" are never shifted, so it is optional for them. The viewer's own time zone is never used.

kpi.description: Optional headline value shown above the chart, with an optional change against a comparison value.

value.description: The headline value, in the same units as the series, as format says (minor or major currency units, ratio or percent). A finite number. Between -1e15 and 1e15; give larger values in a larger unit (thousands or millions).

basis.description: Required. How value relates to the primary series: "total" (its sum), "latest" (its last value), "average" (its mean), or "custom" for a figure computed elsewhere. Forecast points are not actual values, so the first three leave them out; incomplete points count. For those three, value is checked against the primary series, and comparisonValue against the first comparison series over the same slots (like periods: for "latest", the comparison's value where the primary's latest actual value is, even if a plan runs on past it), within 0.5% or one display unit, whichever is larger.

comparisonValue.description: Optional value to compare against, for example the same period last year. The change is shown as a signed percentage, relative even for percent values; it is omitted when this is missing or 0. Between -1e15 and 1e15; give larger values in a larger unit (thousands or millions).

goodDirection.description: Which way a change is good: "up" (revenue) colours rises as good, "down" (churn, dispute or refund rate) colours falls as good. Defaults to "up".

notation.description: How the value is written: "standard" in full ($294,470), or "compact" abbreviated ($294K, $3.8M) as the locale abbreviates. Values under 1,000 and percentages are always written in full, since abbreviating would round them. Defaults to "standard".

type.description: "line" for trends, "bar" for per-day totals, or "kpi" for a headline tile: the KPI value without axes, with a small sparkline of series when given.

stacking.description: How bar series share a slot: "grouped" draws them side by side; "stacked" draws them on top of each other, positive values upward from 0 and negative values downward, so the bar shows the total. Only allowed when type is "bar". Comparison series cannot be stacked. Defaults to "grouped".

legend.description: When the legend shows: "auto" for 3 or more series, or whenever a forecast or projected values need explaining; "show" always; "hide" never. Legend items toggle their series (click, Enter or Space) and isolate it (double-click or Shift+Enter). Defaults to "auto".

labels.description: Label granularity: "auto" picks hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years from the data and width; "day", "month", "year" or "time" force one, still thinned to fit. Defaults to "auto".

notation.description: How labels are written: "compact" ($300K) or "standard" ($300,000). Defaults to "compact".

maximumFractionDigits.description: Most decimals in a label, 0 to 20. Defaults to the fewest that keep ticks exact.

incomplete.description: A trailing period whose data is not final yet, such as today. From from to the end, lines are dashed and bars hatched, and the period is marked with message.

from.description: The first incomplete slot: an x value of the primary series, exactly as written there. Must come before any forecast points.

message.description: Shown for the period. Plain text, up to 200 characters. Defaults to "Data in this period is still being processed".

series.description: 1 to 12 series to plot. Required unless chart.type is "kpi" or loading is true; on a "kpi" chart they are optional and drawn as a sparkline beside the value. Put the primary series (for example this year) first and mark others such as last year with "comparison": true. Series are aligned by position; they may have different lengths. If every series has an empty data array, the card shows emptyMessage.

items.description: One line or set of bars.

label.description: Series name shown in the tooltip and the chart's accessible summary, for example "2026". Plain text.

comparison.description: true to draw this series in the muted comparison style, for example last year. Defaults to false.

color.description: The series color, #rgb or #rrggbb hex, used for its marks, legend swatch, tooltip swatch, sparkline. Defaults to the palette; prefer it, and check contrast if you set one.

data.description: Up to 1000 points in display order. Index i of this series is drawn in the same x slot as index i of every other series. The x-axis labels and the tooltip header come from the first non-comparison series; tooltip rows show each series' label and value, without dates.

x.description: The point's date: "YYYY-MM-DD" for a calendar day (never shifted by time zone), or an ISO 8601 date-time with "Z" or an offset, for example "2026-11-27T18:00:00Z", shown in timeZone. Every x in a chart uses the same form, all dates or all date-times, and years start at 1000. The primary series' dates label the x axis and the tooltip header; a comparison point's own date is read out in the accessible summary.

y.description: The value, in the units format says (minor or major currency units, ratio or percent), or null for a gap. Must be a JSON number, not a string. For a forecast point, the expected value. Between -1e15 and 1e15; give larger values in a larger unit (thousands or millions).

color.description: Bar charts only: this bar segment's color, overriding the series color. #rgb or #rrggbb hex. Prefer the default palette; check contrast if you set one.

forecast.description: true for a forecast rather than an actual value. Forecast points must be one run at the end of the series. Lines draw them dashed from the last actual point; bars as outlined, lightly filled bars. Defaults to false.

low.description: Forecast points only: the lower bound of the forecast range, at most y. Lines shade the band between low and high.

high.description: Forecast points only: the upper bound of the forecast range, at least y.

projected.description: Incomplete points only (from chart.incomplete.from on, in a non-comparison series): where the period is on pace to end, in the same units as y and with the same sign. y stays the value so far, which kpi.basis uses; the chart draws the projection as an extension.

loading.description: true while data is being fetched; series and kpi may then be omitted. Without data, the card shows a placeholder shaped by chart.type; with data (given in series, or already shown by a previous render), the chart stays in place, dimmed, until you render again without loading. Defaults to false.

emptyMessage.description: Message for an empty plot, in your language, for example "No disputes this week". Plain text. Defaults to "No data".

annotations.description: Up to 10 notes on the chart, shown in the tooltip of the slots they cover and the accessible summary. Each uses exactly one of at (a marker) or from/to (a shaded range); x values must be exact x values of the primary series, since series line up by position.

label.description: Short label, for example "Campaign launch". Plain text, up to 80 characters.

description.description: Longer note shown in the tooltip. Plain text, up to 200 characters.

at.description: A single slot: a vertical marker there, or with series a hollow circle in that series color.

from.description: Start of a shaded range, marked with a dashed line; omit to extend to the plot edge.

to.description: End of a shaded range, inclusive, marked with a dashed line; omit to extend to the plot edge.

series.description: With at: the label of the series whose point is marked.
